body:
## Goal

Implement the owner-approved minimal orchestration tools / on-demand Sideagent design. Keep Host context focused on objectives and decisions; retrieve detailed facts when needed. Improve durable handling of new owner directions without duplicate records, persistent assistants, or semantic hard gates. Validate it in a useful live run, not only prompt assertions.

The owner approved implementation after discussion with outer Delegator and Claude Opus Extra High. This issue is the current consolidated scope; earlier research documents' design-only restrictions and unresolved choice lists are superseded here. No release or installation is requested by this issue.

## Agreed design

### Roles and one writer per record

- Delegator owns its existing `.kaola/delegator-heartbeat.json`: owner goals, grants, changes awaiting adoption, cadence and stop boundary. It directly relays owner instructions and monitors.
- Host alone owns `.kaola/heartbeat-prompt.json`: current objective, authority/class/capability summary, outstanding duties, minimal in-flight/recovery locators and adopted decisions. Host owns final allocation, dispatch and acceptance.
- Sideagent is optional and short-lived. It can draft allocation, reconcile a large/conflicting change set, check omissions, synthesize or do explicitly scoped light work. It recommends; it does not grant authority, dispatch independently, accept the project, write either control JSON, or run a scheduler.
- Workflow's run Main Orchestrator remains the sole writer of that run's mission ledger. Forge, Workflow, Git, Runner receipts and dispatch index keep their existing distinct meanings.
- Sideagent does not maintain a separate long-term project state or copy its context into another ledger. Preserve useful conclusions, sources and output files; Host records adopted decisions. Native session history remains native. Do not remove the only recovery anchor when compacting.

### On-demand orchestration operations

Reuse the existing `project` / `execute` / `collect` / `snapshot` entry and Runner primitives. Provide compact read-only views for the demonstrated repeated work: current seats/occupancy against supplied grants, and one exact dispatched turn's outcome/permission/failure evidence. Prefer extending existing output/operations where sufficient; `seats` and `turn` are illustrative names, not a mandatory new command family.

Views are computed from current identity-bound facts, with source/as-of and explicit unknown reasons; they persist no second registry/state and return no authorization or acceptance verdict. Bounded output must not hide failure/permission evidence from the requested cursor range; keep raw receipt pointers and truncation visible. Reuse existing readers/correlation, not a new engine or classifier.

For a nontrivial allocation, Host describes outcome, required abilities, constraints and expected artifacts. Sideagent may use the current authorized/available candidates and profiles to recommend useful worker count, exact presets, bounded assignments and ownership. Host adopts/adjusts the proposal, then existing tools execute. A simple exact dispatch can skip Sideagent. Do not invent parallel work to fill seats or force model balance. Preserve current execute scope restrictions (no expansion to production-mutation fan-out).

### Read/write timing and concise context

- A new Host turn or context recovery loads the compact current state as needed; do not redundantly reload state already read in the same active turn.
- A Runner return is handled from its correlated receipt; it does not require rereading the full heartbeat JSON after every call.
- At a relevant claim, dispatch, plan-adoption or acceptance decision, fetch only fresh facts that can affect it (pending owner changes, candidate details, task evidence). Do not mechanically sweep all state at every event.
- Update Host state when current facts/duties change. No read-back loop after every write. Detailed profiles/worker observations/history stay on demand; essential authority, objectives, pending QA/docs and recovery anchors remain durable.

### Owner changes and adoption

Direct relay remains responsible for delivery: idle send, native noninterrupting steer when supported, otherwise preserve the change until idle. Urgent scoped stop/revocation uses the existing immediate interrupt route, not Sideagent or delayed reads.

Delegator records scoped source-backed pending changes in its existing snapshot and retains them until adoption is evidenced. Host may read relevant pending changes at natural decision boundaries to avoid waiting for the outer timer. Host adopts into its own body; Delegator observes that evidence and confirms/compacts its own record. Neither writes the other's file.

Admission, end-turn, file read or Sideagent receipt alone do not prove adoption. For ordinary changes, a scoped adopted value/duty with source correlation can suffice without a mandatory extra reply; identical values do not prove a one-shot action was performed. Urgent stops retain actual cessation evidence.

Authority and scope precede time. Later explicit owner direction may supersede earlier direction, including reauthorization after a stop. A stale Sideagent draft cannot overwrite newer grants or a runtime revocation. Re-evaluate only affected items. A trusted Delegator relay is valid evidence without a mandatory verbatim-quote gate. Missing/unreadable snapshot means absent/unknown, not proof of no Delegator or no changes; direct delivery still works. Preserve independent pending actions and partial effects; do not collapse them into one scalar or claim exactly-once delivery.

### Resilience and footprint

Use existing records to recover ambiguous sends, partial fan-out, Host/Sideagent interruption and stale drafts without replaying admitted work. Failures stay scoped; unaffected authorized work continues. Existing class-specific limit/account handling and no-login rules stay unchanged.

No second ledger, stored relay queue, marker/revision-counter protocol, background daemon, fixed extra QA seat or compulsory Sideagent. Replace redundant guidance through source templates, regenerate outputs and keep existing byte budgets. Do not move detailed procedures into the main entry or erase established lifecycle/permission rules to make room.

## QA and acceptance

Host owns QA and can delegate bounded checks to suitable authorized workers. Use existing checks plus focused regression for actual changed behavior. No repeated full suite without an affected-evidence reason.

1. Review source/generated guidance consistency: ownership, progressive exposure, class/grant/selection semantics, task lifecycle, no-login/limit handling and existing transport behavior remain intact. Report bytes added/removed by relevant surface; no budget increase.
2. Test compact views against existing real/fixture evidence: exact identity/cursor, unknown/missing source, partial/stopped result, failure/permission evidence outside shortened reply, no mutation/new stored state. Reuse appropriate tests.
3. Run one useful bounded live QA/research assignment using candidate code/guidance: Host describes needs; on-demand Sideagent recommends from actual authorized/available presets; Host adopts and dispatches through existing supported scope; results correlate; Host ends the active turn while workers run, handles completion, judges results and stops finished workers. Show concise existing start/send/output/stop evidence. Do not reuse finished sessions just to save a start.
4. Exercise pending-update/stale-proposal and interrupted/partial recovery semantics using safe scoped QA fixtures where needed. A test direction is not real new authority. Observe actual model behavior where possible; label fixture-only or unobserved branches honestly. No user-stop experiment against unrelated work, manufactured credential failure, new permission, or global installation.
5. Compare routine bytes/read calls/duplicated facts before vs after on the useful trial. Token/cost/latency savings may be claimed only with measurements; include Sideagent overhead. Preserve failures and resulting corrections, not a zero-risk guarantee.
6. Host delivers integrated candidate, QA verdict, limitations and normal Workflow closeout. Outer Delegator personally reviews implementation against this scope and the real-run evidence before final closeout; repair concrete gaps only.

## Design references (local supporting evidence, not additional requirements)

- `/tmp/kpr-orchestration-tools-opus-design.md` revision 3
- `/tmp/kpr-orchestration-tools-consensus.md`
- `/tmp/kpr-orchestration-consensus-outer-response.md`
- `/tmp/kpr-information-lifecycle-research.md`

This issue and subsequent explicit owner corrections win over old draft examples, raw-quote requirements, missing-snapshot assumptions and design-only caveats. Baseline main at approval: `987022949d55784c4e0a4138ca3a159315311e85`. The published/installed release remains v0.7.0; do not mistake source inspection for installed Skill loading.


## Latest owner correction — 2026-10-03

Use **Sideagent**, not Sidekick, as the product role name. Apply consistently across current source prompts, generated Skills, README/docs, tool/help/schema/role metadata and tests wherever this role is exposed. This is a terminology change, not a change to allocation, authority, ownership or lifecycle. Inspect existing public consumers/serialized role values before changing machine-facing identifiers; preserve in-flight identity and recoverability and document any necessary narrow compatibility handling. Do not rewrite historical receipts, archived work, native session names or the evidence files referenced above. Keep the source filename/locator valid even when it contains the former name. Include name consistency and affected consumer behavior in existing #252 QA; do not add a new issue or framework.
title: Keep Host orchestration concise with on-demand facts and Sideagent proposals
